unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: the book opens on two datelines in two counting systems - בִּשְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.1.1, a regnal/exilic year the book never names an era for) and הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַחֲמִישִׁ֔ית לְגָל֖וּת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יוֹיָכִֽין (oshb:Ezek.1.2, the fifth year of Jehoiachin's exile) - followed at oshb:Ezek.1.3 by the superscription הָיֹ֣ה הָיָ֣ה דְבַר יְ֠הוָה אֶל יְחֶזְקֵ֨אל, an infinitive-absolute-plus-perfect word-event with a THIRD-PERSON addressee ('to Ezekiel', not 'to me'). This verb and addressee shape are why the verse sits in the 49-verse any-form word-event count and not the 48-verse first-person family (sweep: verses containing the word-event phrase in any form, 49; the 48 excludes this one verse by predicate). It is weighed here as a real onset in its own right, not folded into or discounted against the vision that follows. The same verse also carries וַתְּהִ֥י עָלָ֛יו שָׁ֖ם יַד יְהוָֽה, the hand-of-YHWH construct that opens the book's first vision (one of 7 verses carrying the construct). Close: the scene runs unbroken to oshb:Ezek.1.28, מַרְאֵ֖ה דְּמ֣וּת כְּבוֹד יְהוָ֑ה וָֽאֶרְאֶה֙ וָאֶפֹּ֣ל עַל פָּנַ֔י וָאֶשְׁמַ֖ע ק֥וֹל מְדַבֵּֽר, glossed by the WEB as “This was the appearance of the likeness of Yahweh’s glory. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard a voice of one that spoke” (web:Ezek.1.28). No word-event, messenger, recognition or utterance formula interrupts 1:4-1:27 (the transport-verb and 'he said to me' sweeps that mark scene changes elsewhere in the book's visions do not begin until chapter 8), so the throne-theophany carries no formula-marked internal seam; the samekh recorded after 1:28 and the fresh 'he said to me' that opens oshb:Ezek.2.1 together mark the vision/commission seam on the FAR side of this unit; the onset evidence at oshb:Ezek.2.1 is weighed there.
unchanged_prose_now.strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating oshb:Ezek.1.1-1.3 as its own superscription unit, separate from the vision it introduces. Rejected because the vision proper (1:4-1:28) carries no independent onset device of its own - it simply continues the sentence the hand-of-YHWH clause opens - so cutting after 1:3 would manufacture a seam the bytes do not mark, and would still leave a 25-verse remainder with the same cap problem.
unchanged_prose_now.device_notes: Whole-chapter span (28 verses), well above the 7-10 typical density and above the 14-16 stretch cap for measured/listed blocks even though this is not such a block; disclosed and held at low confidence rather than forced into an unsupported internal cut. MT 1:3 is cited only under the 49-verse any-form word-event count, never blended with the 48-verse first-person family. K/Q at 1:8 checked before quoting: the unit does not splice the disputed word. The OSHB editorial note at 1:11 is disclosed as single-witness apparatus, not a reading change. Paseq at 1:1 and 1:27 disclosed count-only (single-witness); no intra-verse position is claimed.

A pe is recorded after 3:9, כְּשָׁמִ֛יר חָזָ֥ק מִצֹּ֖ר נָתַ֣תִּי מִצְחֶ֑ךָ (“I have made your forehead as a diamond” (web:Ezek.3.9)), closing with a further rebellious-house refrain, כִּ֛י בֵּֽית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.9) (the third of six). That mark is disclosed but not read as the unit's own close: 3:10 reopens with “Moreover he said to me” (web:Ezek.3.10) on the same audience-description topic, and cutting there would leave 3:10-3:11 (2 verses, no word-event of its own) detached from the speech they continue. Close: 3:11, אִֽם יִשְׁמְע֖וּ וְאִם יֶחְדָּֽלוּ (oshb:Ezek.3.11) (“whether they will hear, or whether they will refuse” (web:Ezek.3.11)), immediately before the return-transport of 3:12 begins a distinct, vision-texture scene.
unchanged_prose_now.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting after the pe at 3:9. Rejected because the two verses that would remain, 3:10-3:11, share the same 'he said to me' commissioning texture as 3:4-3:9 with no onset device distinguishing them, and they would stand as a two-verse unit whose opening is a further 'he said to me' in the same speech, with no word-event, hand-of-YHWH construct or dateline of its own (sweep: 0 of the 49 any-form word-event verses, 0 of the 7 hand-of-YHWH verses and 0 of the 14 dateline verses fall in 3:10-3:11).
unchanged_prose_now.device_notes: Paseq at 3:6 disclosed count-only (single-witness); no intra-verse position claimed. The pe following 3:9 is disclosed as single-witness sub-paragraph evidence inside the unit, weighed and not adopted as the cut point for the reason given in boundary_rationale. A pe follows MT 3:3 (single witness), the paragraph mark standing just behind this unit's opening verse.

unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:22 וַתְּהִ֥י עָלַ֛י שָׁ֖ם יַד יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.3.22) (“Yahweh’s hand was there on me” (web:Ezek.3.22)), the hand-of-YHWH construct read here as a genuine vision onset (contrast oshb:Ezek.3.14, where the construct accompanies the spirit carrying the prophet away, a transit rather than a new scene) because it opens a fresh scene: “Arise, go out into the plain” (web:Ezek.3.22). 3:25 announces that עֲבוֹתִ֔ים (oshb:Ezek.3.25) ('ropes') will be put on the prophet; the word recurs at 4:8 in the siege sign-act, across the 3:27/4:1 seam (accent_stripped tier: the same consonants and vowels under a different accent), so the muteness command and the sign-acts share a device, and that continuity is weighed here against the seam even though the unit boundary stands. 3:26 carries the fifth rebellious-house refrain, כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה. Close: 3:27, הַשֹּׁמֵ֤עַ יִשְׁמָע֙ וְהֶחָדֵ֣ל יֶחְדָּ֔ל כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.27) (“He who hears, let him hear; and he who refuses, let him refuse; for they are a rebellious house” (web:Ezek.3.27)) - the sixth verse in chapters 2-3 to name the rebellious house (sweep: 12 verses book-wide name it, six of them in chapters 2-3), and the parent P1's close; a samekh is recorded after this verse. Across the seam, 4:1 opens with וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ (oshb:Ezek.4.1) ('and you, son of man'), spliced at byte tier as the 3:27 clause is, and turns to the command to take a tile, the sub-onset that starts the sign-acts. The unit therefore stops at 3:27 and does not extend into 4:1; the seam's near side is closed by the refrain and the samekh after 3:27 (single witness), and its far side is opened by that sub-onset.
unchanged_prose_now.strongest_rejected_alternative: Placing the P1/P2 parent seam at 3:15/3:16 instead of 3:27/4:1, on the strength of 3:16's own strict word-event and the seven-day close it answers. Weighed on the bytes, the onset side of that seam is strong: 3:16 sets מִקְצֵ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.3.16) (“At the end of seven days” (web:Ezek.3.16)) before its strict word-event, and a pe follows 3:16 itself (single witness), after the word-event verse rather than before it. Its close side is narrative: 3:15 ends the journey to the exiles on seven days of sitting among them, a report rather than a refrain. The rebellious-house refrain runs on both sides of 3:16 (sweep: of the six verses in chapters 2-3 that name the rebellious house, four stand before 3:16 and two after it), so a parent seam there would divide that series, whereas at 3:27/4:1 the series' sixth verse stands on the close side and the sub-onset of 4:1 on the onset side. The alternative is kept as a held question and not argued away, because the ropes of 3:25, taken up at 4:8, tie the muteness command (3:22-27) to the sign-acts (4:1-17) across the later seam.

unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: 6:1 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.6.1) ('Yahweh's word came to me, saying'), a strict word-event, hard seam. 6:2 opens the oracle's direction with שִׂ֥ים פָּנֶ֖יךָ אֶל הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.6.2) (“set your face toward the mountains of Israel” (web:Ezek.6.2)). A 2mp recognition-family close occurs mid-unit at 6:7, וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.6.7) ('and you shall know that I am Yahweh'); it is disclosed but read as paragraph-final rather than unit-final, since 6:8 continues without a fresh onset device (“Yet I will leave a remnant” (web:Ezek.6.8)). Close: 6:10, the strict recognition formula וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.6.10) ('and they shall know that I am Yahweh'), with a pe recorded after it, immediately before a fresh messenger formula reopens the address at 6:11.
unchanged_prose_now.strongest_rejected_alternative: Closing the unit at 6:7, the first recognition occurrence, rather than continuing to 6:10. Rejected because 6:8's “Yet I will leave a remnant” (web:Ezek.6.8) carries straight on from 6:7 with no messenger formula, word-event or address restarting the speech, so 6:7 reads as an internal refrain rather than the unit's own close.

peer_03_row_item.why_from_the_bytes: MEASURED from pmarks_Ezek.json at its pinned digest: a PE is recorded on Ezek.14.1, and the file's own marks_note states the convention - 'SAMEKH = setumah (closed section), PE = petuchah (open section), recorded on the verse the mark FOLLOWS'. Ezek.14.1 is this row's FIRST verse. C1 verbatim: 'A mark recorded on a row's FIRST verse stands inside the row (after that verse) and can never corroborate the row's onset.' The row does the opposite in three places - in its boundary_rationale ('a pe follows this very verse ... the scene-onset is pe-corroborated even without a formula'), in its first boundary_evidence_refs entry ('pe follows; opens this row'), and in its rejected-alternative field ('the pe following 14:1 corroborates keeping the elders'-scene verse inside this row'). The row states the mark's POSITION correctly and then infers the opposite DIRECTION from it, which is exactly the disclosure defect C1 names. MARKS-3D adds a second consequence: 'inside the span' means first verse through last-but-one, so the PE on Ezek.14.1 is an INTERIOR mark, weighed and never cutting alone - and the row's device_notes disclose only 'three mid-row samekh marks' at Ezek.14.3, 14.5 and 14.8, so the interior mark count is stated as three when it is MEASURED four. A10 bites as well: the previous recorded mark is the SAMEKH on Ezek.13.19, so the witness's own paragraph runs MT 13:20-14:1 (MEASURED), which groups Ezek.14.1 with what precedes; A10 requires that a disagreeing sectioning be 'stated as evidence against the row, never reread to agree with it'. A9 is formally satisfied and substantively inverted: the division after Ezek.14.1 stands exactly at the cut the row rejects, which is opening at 14:2, and the row names it in the rejected-alternative field but weighs it as evidence AGAINST that cut. OL found none of this; its item instead repeats the row's framing - 'The row's own frame holds on both sides: a petuchah is recorded after MT 14:1, the span's opening verse, and again after MT 14:11' - which states the position correctly and then treats an interior mark as framing. Two correlated lanes split here, and the ruling decides it for LF. OL's own finding is nevertheless genuine and I confirm it: MEASURED, oshb:Ezek.14.8 ends on the 2mp recognition refrain, a member of my re-derived 2mp-21 and wider-64 and therefore refrain-grade under the strategy's rule, and it also carries the mashal token, being one of the 11 verses my own mashal re-derivation returns; the SAMEKH recorded on Ezek.14.8 therefore follows a refrain-grade close, and the row discloses that mark as a bare 'mid-row' with neither device named.

unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: 23:36 is a sub-onset — "YHWH said to me" plus the "son of man" address, judging BOTH sisters together (dual/plural addressee, a shift from the prior unit's singular Oholibah address) — whole verse = "וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י בֶּן אָדָ֕ם הֲתִשְׁפּ֥וֹט אֶֽת אָהֳלָ֖ה וְאֶת אָהֳלִיבָ֑ה וְהַגֵּ֣ד לָהֶ֔ן אֵ֖ת תוֹעֲבוֹתֵיהֶֽן (oshb:Ezek.23.36)". This is not a hard seam (the hard seams inside this collection are the dateline and word-event onsets at 22:1, 22:17, 22:23, 23:1, 24:1 and 24:15; 23:36 is not among them); it is instead a held either/or question — its own unit, or the close of the 23:1-35 allegory — rather than a hard seam. Close: 23:49, whole verse = "וְנָתְנ֤וּ זִמַּתְכֶ֨נָה֙ עֲלֵיכֶ֔ן וַחֲטָאֵ֥י גִלּוּלֵיכֶ֖ן תִּשֶּׂ֑אינָה וִידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.23.49)" — ending in a recognition-formula-pattern clause (2mp verb form with the "Lord YHWH" divine-name variant, read directly from these bytes rather than from any pre-counted inventory list), followed by a pe mark (single-witness).
unchanged_prose_now.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 23:36-49 as the CLOSE of the single 23:1-49 allegory rather than its own unit — this is a live alternative and it is not dismissed here, only not taken: 23:36's combination of a fresh address formula and an addressee-count shift is read as closer in kind to a fresh unit-opening than to a coda, so it is written as its own unit, held at medium confidence rather than high.
unchanged_prose_now.device_notes: One ketiv/qere note sits at 23:42, left unquoted here. 23:43 is a doubled-note verse — TWO separate ketiv/qere pairs on the one verse, one of 23 such doubled verses across the book — and both are left to the K/Q layer's own record rather than spliced in here, since a hand-split of the raw ketiv-plus-qere field risks an easy byte error.

boundary_rationale.before: Onset: 25:1 opens with the word-event formula, "וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.25.1) — the strict 39-form and the any-form 41-count both, carrying no dateline. In the WEB, “Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,” (web:Ezek.25.1). 25:2 supplies the addressee, "בֶּן אָדָ֕ם שִׂ֥ים פָּנֶ֖יךָ אֶל בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן וְהִנָּבֵ֖א עֲלֵיהֶֽם" (oshb:Ezek.25.2) — the set-your-face command “toward the children of Ammon” (web:Ezek.25.2, WEB) is the book's first foreign addressee, the class shift that opens the oracles-against-the-nations collection. Close (weighed from both sides): 25:7 ends "לָכֵ֡ן הִנְנִי֩ נָטִ֨יתִי אֶת יָדִ֜י עָלֶ֗יךָ וּנְתַתִּ֤יךָֽ לבג לַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְהִכְרַתִּ֨יךָ֙ מִן הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֖יךָ מִן הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת אַשְׁמִ֣ידְךָ֔ וְיָדַעְתָּ֖ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.7; לבג there is the verse’s ketiv, Qere לְבַז֙), closing on the 2ms recognition variant "and you shall know that I am YHWH" with a SAMEKH immediately after. An earlier internal close sits at 25:5, "וְנָתַתִּ֤י אֶת רַבָּה֙ לִנְוֵ֣ה גְמַלִּ֔ים וְאֶת בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן לְמִרְבַּץ צֹ֑אן וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.5), which also ends on a 2mp recognition-family clause (the wider 2mp recognition family, sweep: 21 verses, includes 25:5, not the strict 2ms list, sweep: 5 verses) and carries its own SAMEKH. strongest_rejected_alternative.before: Three alternatives are weighed. (1) Ending the row at 29:6, where an extended (non-strict) recognition-type close occurs; rejected because 29:7 continues the same staff-of-reed image with no intervening onset, and because this chapter's own onset/close collision pattern places the true seam after 29:9, not 29:6. Two further readings are weighed, as ordered. (2) Cutting at 29:7/29:8 - the alternative the paragraph layer proposes, carrying the ordered A10 mark disclosure. A10: MEASURED from the section-mark record, MT 29:7 is followed by a SAMEKH (setumah, closed section, single-witness), recorded on the verse it follows, and MT 29:7 additionally carries one ketiv/qere pair, already disclosed in this row. What the rival's near face carries: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, MT 29:8 opens on the long-form messenger formula after a therefore-particle (oshb:Ezek.29.8), and with it a grammatical addressee shift - MT 29:7 addresses a masculine singular and MT 29:8 a feminine singular (oshb:Ezek.29.7, oshb:Ezek.29.8), that is, from Pharaoh to the land. Whether CUT-RULE licenses it: limb (a) IS satisfied on that addressee change, so this rival is licensed and two-faced and is not dismissed. Its far face is nevertheless thin: MT 29:7 ends with no close-role formula, so limb (b) would fail there and only the SAMEKH stands. The stated ground on which this row holds: the crocodile verdict's own refrain is the recognition formula at MT 29:9, and MT 29:10 restates the same charge as a fresh against-you cycle (oshb:Ezek.29.10); a licensed text signal outranking a section mark the SAMEKH after MT 29:7 is weak corroboration and is disclosed FOR this rival, not for this row. A licensed two-faced rival held on stated grounds is CONF-CAL's MEDIUM limb, which is where this row's grade now sits. What supports it: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, no dateline and no word-event formula stands anywhere between MT 29:1 and the next dateline at MT 29:17; MEASURED from the section-mark record, the only marks inside that stretch follow MT 29:7 and MT 29:12, and NO mark stands on MT 29:9. unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: the strict word-event formula opens the Gog complex at oshb:Ezek.38.1 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (sweep: 39 verses strict form), immediately corroborated by the set-your-face direction opener at oshb:Ezek.38.2 בֶּן אָדָ֗ם שִׂ֤ים פָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶל גּוֹג֙ אֶ֣רֶץ הַמָּג֔וֹג נְשִׂ֕יא רֹ֖אשׁ מֶ֣שֶׁךְ וְתֻבָ֑ל וְהִנָּבֵ֖א עָלָֽיו (sweep: 9 verses book-wide) and the messenger formula naming the addressee at oshb:Ezek.38.3. The unit runs as a paragraph chain rather than four separate rows: the messenger-formula reopenings at oshb:Ezek.38.10, oshb:Ezek.38.14 and oshb:Ezek.38.17 each change no addressee -- Gog stands as the referent throughout -- and none follows a refrain; the samekh marks recorded after oshb:Ezek.38.9, oshb:Ezek.38.13, oshb:Ezek.38.16 and oshb:Ezek.38.17 (four samekh, tier-3 single-witness) therefore mark internal paragraphs rather than row seams, including a one-verse Masoretic paragraph at 38.17 itself. Two utterance-formula closes fall mid-unit at oshb:Ezek.38.18 and oshb:Ezek.38.21; both are paragraph-final rather than row-final because no fresh onset of the tracked classes follows either one, and the catastrophe description runs on without interruption. Close: the strict recognition formula closes the whole chapter at oshb:Ezek.38.23 וְהִתְגַּדִּלְתִּי֙ וְהִתְקַדִּשְׁתִּ֔י וְנ֣וֹדַעְתִּ֔י לְעֵינֵ֖י גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֑ים וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (sweep: 28 verses strict form), with a samekh mark recorded immediately after -- a refrain-grade close corroborated by a masoretic mark, weighed against the son-of-man sub-onset that opens the following material at oshb:Ezek.39.1.
unchanged_prose_now.strongest_rejected_alternative: The four paragraph rows Ezek.38.1-Ezek.38.9, Ezek.38.10-Ezek.38.13, Ezek.38.14-Ezek.38.16 and Ezek.38.17-Ezek.38.23, cut at each messenger-formula reopening (38.10, 38.14, 38.17). Rejected: none of those reopenings changes the addressee (Gog stands as referent throughout the chapter) and none follows a refrain-grade close -- the samekh marks after 38.9, 38.13, 38.16 and 38.17 correspond to paragraph breaks the tradition itself records without a matching formula seam, so, since a messenger formula is cut only on an addressee change or a preceding refrain, the four spans stay inside one row.
unchanged_prose_now.device_notes: Whole-chapter row (Ezek.38.1-38.23, 23 verses): held at medium_low as a whole-chapter span, disclosed rather than assumed, since no formula seam divides the mobilization, the plan, the traders' challenge and the prophets' testimony from the day-of-defeat oracle. Four samekh marks stand after 38.9, 38.13, 38.16 and 38.17 (tier-3 single-witness); the mark after 38.17 makes it a one-verse Masoretic paragraph, disclosed here and not read as an internal cut, since isolating it alone would leave a row with no content beyond its own onset formula. Paseq occurrences (count-only, single-witness) fall at 38.8 (two), 38.10, 38.13, 38.14, 38.18 and 38.19; no K/Q note falls in this span. 38.4 carries an OSHB editorial note recording an accent divergence from BHS (single-witness apparatus, not a text variant).

unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 40:1 opens with the dateline בְּאַרְבַּ֤ע עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה אַחַ֕ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֻכְּתָ֖ה הָעִ֑יר (“after the city was struck” (web:Ezek.40.1)) -- the fourteenth and last of the book's fourteen year-bearing datelines -- paired in the same verse with the hand-of-YHWH idiom הָיְתָ֤ה עָלַי֙ יַד יְהוָ֔ה and the transport verb וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתִ֖י שָֽׁמָּה (oshb:Ezek.40.1). This dateline-hand-transport cluster is the strongest onset class the book offers and is also a HARD seam: no row may cross it. It follows immediately, without intervening material, the utterance formula and pe (oshb:Ezek.39.29, single-witness) that close the preceding unit. The frame continues at 40:2 with the header בְּמַרְא֣וֹת אֱלֹהִ֔ים “In the visions of God” (web:Ezek.40.2; one of only three such headers in the book) plus a further transport pair (הֱבִיאַ֖נִי / וַיְנִיחֵ֗נִי (oshb:Ezek.40.2)), and again at 40:3 (וַיָּבֵ֨יא אוֹתִ֜י שָׁ֗מָּה (oshb:Ezek.40.3)) introducing the measuring man. Close side: 40:4 carries no formula-grade close device; the seam at 40:4/40:5 rests on the man's charge, הַגֵּ֛ד אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.40.4) “Declare all that you see to the house of Israel.” (web:Ezek.40.4), read as ending the entry scene before the measuring reed is put to use in 40:5's וַיָּ֜מָד (oshb:Ezek.40.5), the first of an eighteen-verse run of that verb across 40:5-41:5. Both sides are weighed: the onset is the best-evidenced in the whole span; the close is a content judgment (charge-speech versus measuring-action), not a refrain, and is held accordingly.

unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: no formula device opens Ezek.45.1 ('and when you divide the land by lot' is a continuation clause, not a word-event, son-of-man address or messenger formula); the row follows directly after the pe recorded after Ezek.44.31. This is the held 44.31/45.1 question: the priests' portion at 44.28-31 is taken as the true close of the prior unit (its own pe is the nearest mark), and 45.1 is read as opening a new one on content grounds alone -- the sanctuary-and-prince land allotment, a distinct topic from priestly dues. The row covers the holy portion's dimensions (1-3), the priests' land (4), the Levites' land (5), the city's possession (6), and the prince's portion (7-8). Close: the samekh recorded after Ezek.45.8 gives this stretch a real parashah-marked close even though its onset carries none; the following verse, 45.9, opens with a fresh messenger formula on a different topic (weights and measures).
unchanged_prose_now.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 45.1-8 into the temple-law material before it (44.15-31) as a continuation of ch44's priestly-portions material (no seam at all before 44.31/45.1, running the law section straight through). Rejected because the topic shifts cleanly from priestly dues to land-allotment dimensions, and because the samekh at 45.8 gives this stretch its own marked close, which a run-on unit would leave unexplained.
unchanged_prose_now.device_notes: No onset formula at Ezek.45.1; this row is held on content grounds and the Ezek.45.8 samekh alone, both disclosed. Ezek.45.1 carries a paseq (count-only, single-witness; intra-verse position unsourceable from the verse text).

A samekh mark is recorded after Ezek.46.19 itself -- one verse INTO this row, not at its outer boundary -- disclosed as mid-unit texture that does not cut, since the transport-and-explanation sequence at 46.19-20 reads as one scene and no fresh formula or addressee shift accompanies the mark. unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: the list heading וְאֵ֖לֶּה שְׁמ֣וֹת (oshb:Ezek.48.1), 'these are the names', opens the row as the list's own onset device; the seam behind it at 47.23/48.1 is argued from the Ezek.47.23 close (utterance + samekh, a doubled close signal seen again, with a pe, at 48.29) and the topic shift from border-division instruction to the tribal-portion list itself. The row covers the seven northern tribal portions in the 'one portion' refrain, Dan through Judah (1-7), each closing on its own 'one portion' formula; no cut falls inside this refrain block. Close: Ezek.48.7 closes the northern block on its own 'one portion' formula; the next verse, 48.8, turns from the tribal-portion list to the holy offering on a change of listed object -- a distinct topic that opens no formula of its own but marks a real content seam at the list's own internal division.
unchanged_prose_now.strongest_rejected_alternative: The single 48.1-29 row spanning the entire tribal-portion list, holy portion, city, and prince's land as one unit. Rejected because the 29-verse span exceeds every cap without a formula-less stretch forcing it, and the list's own internal divisions -- the change of listed object at 48.8 and the list-resumption formula at 48.23 -- give real, though formula-free, content seams that a single row would leave undisclosed.
unchanged_prose_now.device_notes: The 'one portion' refrain block 48.1-7 is never cut inside. A paseq is recorded within Ezek.48.1 and within Ezek.48.7 (each count-only, single-witness). Held at medium_low.

unchanged_prose_now.device_notes: No formula onset or close marks this row on either side; it is held on content-shift grounds and the book's own coda status.
